content: 1. The proportion of HIV-positive individuals with new or relapsed tuberculosis (TB) who are on antiretroviral therapy (ART) during TB treatment is determined by identifying the number of such patients who were either already on ART or initiated ART during TB treatment within the reporting period. This is compared to the total number of HIV-positive new and relapsed TB patients registered during the same period. Data is collected from TB and ART registers, including information on TB status, HIV care enrollment date, ART start date, and ART follow-up status (e.g., dates of stopping, restarting, or being lost to follow-up). Prompt TB treatment and early ART initiation are critical for reducing mortality and reflect the strength of collaboration between national HIV and TB programs. 2. This is calculated by comparing the number of HIV-positive adults initiating ART within the past 12 months with a baseline CD4 count below 200 to the total number of HIV-positive adults initiating ART within the same period. Data is sourced from ART registers, including ART start dates and baseline CD4 counts. The threshold of <200 cells/μL aligns with the 2016 advanced disease definition by Waldrop et al. 3. ART retention is assessed as the percentage of people living with HIV who remain on ART 12 months after initiation (or at subsequent intervals such as 24, 36, 48, or 60 months). This is calculated by comparing the number of patients alive and on ART at the specified time point to the total number of patients who initiated ART within the corresponding period. The data includes those who have died, stopped treatment, or been lost to follow-up. Information is gathered from ART registers and follow-up records. 4. This is determined by comparing the number of individuals with suppressed viral loads to the total number of people on ART at the end of the reporting period. Data is collected from lab registers, ART registers, and cross-sectional reports. Viral load suppression is the gold standard for assessing ART adherence. If viral load testing coverage is below 75% of those on ART, results should be interpreted cautiously, as recommended by UNAIDS. 5. Cotrimoxazole (CTX) prophylaxis coverage is calculated as the percentage of HIV-exposed infants who are started on CTX prophylaxis within two months of birth. This is determined by comparing the number of HIV-exposed infants born in the past 12 months who started CTX within two months to the total number of HIV-positive women who delivered during the same period. Data is sourced from HIV-exposed infant (HEI) registers, including the date of birth and age at CTX initiation. CTX prophylaxis is essential for reducing opportunistic infections and bacterial infections and serves as a proxy for HEI follow-up. 6. This is calculated by comparing the number of HIV-positive individuals whose TB status was assessed and recorded to the total number of HIV-positive individuals enrolled in HIV care during the same period. Data is collected from ART registers, including TB status, HIV care enrollment dates, and ART follow-up status. 7. Early ART initiation for HIV-positive TB patients is assessed as the proportion of new and relapsed HIV-positive TB patients who start ART within eight weeks of their TB diagnosis. This is calculated by comparing the number of such patients who initiated ART within eight weeks to the total number of HIV-positive new and relapsed TB patients detected during the reporting period who were not already on ART. Data is collected from HIV patient cards or ART registers, reconciled with TB registers. Early ART initiation significantly improves survival and quality of life for TB patients living with HIV, though it may require intensive labor to track and document. 8. This is calculated by comparing the number of individuals with viral load test results at 12 months to the total number of individuals alive and on ART at the same time point. Data is sourced from lab registers, ART registers, and cohort reports. 9. ART survival is assessed as the percentage of people living with HIV who are alive at 12, 24, 36 months, etc., after initiating ART. This is calculated by comparing the number of individuals alive and on ART at the specified time points to the total number of individuals who initiated ART within the corresponding period. The numerator has been revised to include only those who are alive and on ART. Data is collected from ART registers, and aggregation across service delivery points may be necessary.
